_comment: Approximate teaspoons per one native container unit, for ingredients the source ships as a pre-portioned dose (a sachet of spice mix, a pot of curry powder). HelloFresh states no quantity at all for these: with a meal kit the instruction is 'add the sachet' and it is self-executing, but shopping at a supermarket the cook holds a 40g jar and has to measure. Spoons are the actionable unit at the hob, and because sachets are portion-filled by volume rather than weighed, unit->volume is far more stable across spices than unit->mass, which needs a density per spice. Estimates, not measurements: the generic by_unit figures assume a mid-density ground spice (~2.3 g/tsp) at the gram weights in ingredient_grams.json, and by_name overrides carry the low-density dried leaf herbs, whose sachets hold far fewer grams for the same fill. Where a spice is potent enough that overdoing it ruins the dish (see ingredient_potency.json), the by_name figure deliberately errs low: an under-seasoned dish is corrected at the table, an over-cinnamoned one is not, so the asymmetry in the cost of being wrong is worth paying for in the estimate. Resolution: exact by_name -> first substring in by_keyword -> generic by_unit -> null. See app/measures.py.
